title: Config diff collector: routing policy + feature flags with redaction + allowlisted keys
author: Jacob Stein
release_notes: Incident bot can now attach a time-bounded config diff (effective routing policy + feature flags) with redaction and restricted posting guardrails.
description: Motivation: During multiple incidents (e.g., SUP-4970 and pm follow-ups), responders lacked fast visibility into whether a recent routing/policy change or flag flip likely caused the degradation. This PR adds a new collector that fetches effective config snapshots at two timepoints (t-30m and now by default), computes a stable diff, and posts a compact summary block into the incident thread. Scope: (1) New ConfigDiffCollector implementation (policy bundle + feature flags). (2) Redaction + safe-to-post classification, with an allowlist-driven model. (3) Example outputs + formatting tuned for Slack readability. (4) Guardrails: bounded latency, partial rendering, and restricted-mode support (collector produces both a 'public' and 'restricted' rendering). Data sources: config snapshot endpoint (region-aware) and flag service read API; both are called through existing incident-bot HTTP client with per-request deadlines. Redaction model: keys are classified as SAFE, SENSITIVE, or UNKNOWN based on allowlists/denylists. SAFE keys render full old/new values. SENSITIVE keys render 'changed' with hashed fingerprints (sha256 truncated) and value length only. UNKNOWN keys do not render values; the collector emits a single summary line 'N unknown keys changed (see restricted bundle or request escalation)'. If restricted mode is enabled for the incident, the collector includes additional context in the restricted bundle, but still redacts obvious secrets (tokens, JWTs, API keys) and strips any fields matching common secret patterns. Output format: The collector emits (a) 'Config changes (last 30m)' header, (b) top changes grouped by domain (routing / rate-limits / autoscaling / flags), (c) links: config snapshot diff view + runbook 'Triage with deploy + config context', and (d) a footer with snapshot timestamps/regions and any redaction notes. Example snippet (public): 'routing.policy.default_model: redwood/llama-3.1-70b -> redwood/llama-3.1-70b-quant (region=us-east)'; 'flags.enable_kv_cache_v2: false -> true'; 'routing.customer_overrides[*]: 2 keys changed (sensitive)'. Failure modes: if one snapshot fetch fails, collector posts 'Config diff unavailable' with cause category (timeout / auth / upstream 5xx) and provides a manual command hint '/incident-bot config-diff --region us-east --window 30m'. Collector fails open and never blocks other collectors. Testing: unit tests cover canonicalization (stable ordering), diff correctness, allowlist/denylist behavior, secret pattern redaction, and slack rendering. Added golden tests for example policy bundles and flag snapshots. Also added lightweight contract test verifying we don’t log raw config values at INFO. Rollout: behind 'incident_bot.collectors.config_diff.enabled' (default false). Per-channel allowlist and restricted-mode routing is handled by existing posting layer; this collector produces both renderings and relies on the poster to select where to send them.
commits: collector: add config snapshot + flag snapshot clients with timeouts
security: add key allowlist/denylist + secret pattern scrubber
render: slack blocks for config diff summary + redaction notices
tests: golden fixtures for policy bundles + flags + redaction behavior
docs: update incident-bot collector registry + usage examples
conversation: Rafael Mendes (review): The diff output looks good, but I’m worried about value leaks in Slack. Can we guarantee we never post customer-specific routing override values? Jacob Stein (author): Yes — added domain-based denylist for routing.customer_overrides and any key containing 'override', 'token', 'secret', 'jwt', 'api_key'. Those render as 'changed (sensitive)' with fingerprints only. Also added an UNKNOWN bucket that never prints values unless key is explicitly allowlisted. Ethan Park (review): Snapshot fetch: are we hitting the config service too frequently during big incidents? Jacob Stein: Collector memoizes per (incident_id, region, window, timestamp_bucket=5m) via existing collector cache; worst case one fetch per region per 5 minutes. Also added per-request timeout 900ms and overall collector budget 2s. Mina Haddad (review): For routing policies, we should include the effective default model and fallback policy changes above-the-fold. Right now flags can push the important stuff down. Jacob Stein: Reordered grouping to always render routing first, then rate-limits/autoscaling, then flags. Also added heuristic to bubble keys matching 'default_model', 'fallback', 'region_weights', 'max_concurrent_requests'. Marcus Lin (security review): Two asks before approval: (1) Ensure logs never include raw config values, including error paths. (2) Denylist should include 'headers' and 'webhook'. Jacob Stein: Added INFO log scrubber (only key names + counts) and made error logs include only status code + request id. Added 'headers' and 'webhook' patterns. Added unit tests verifying redaction on error rendering and a grep-based test to prevent 'snapshot_now' payload logging. Allison Grant (review): Can we attach a link to the canonical dashboard or diff viewer so responders can dig deeper without asking the bot to print more? Jacob Stein: Added link fields: 'Config snapshots' deep link (policy diff view) and the runbook 'Triage with deploy + config context'. Also added a hint in the footer to request restricted bundle if needed. Outcome: Approved after changes; squashed and merged.
notes: Follow-ups: (1) Align allowlist keys with Platform policy bundle schema v2 once available. (2) Add integration test using recorded fixtures from real incidents (planned in ENG-2849). (3) Confirm restricted-mode channel routing in pr_0128; this collector already emits restricted rendering but relies on poster config.
